questions.prompt: A friction coefficient of 0.4 is uncertain by a factor of 2. What is the upper end of its range? (one decimal)
Four randomized parameters, each with 3 grid values. How many grid points?
Random samples needed so that the probability of missing a region of 10% of the volume is at most 5% (round up)?
A randomized policy has the same mean cost inside the box as a nominal policy but a much lower worst-case cost on held-out corners. This shows
options: that the nominal policy is better
robustness that the mean cost alone hides
questions.explanation: Equal means can hide very different tails; the held-out worst case is where the difference shows.

questions.prompt: Controller A costs (0.24, 0.30, 1.17) on three plants and B costs (0.60, 0.68, 0.78). What is the worst-case cost of the better worst-case controller? (two decimals)
questions.explanation: max A = 1.17, max B = 0.78; B has the lower worst case.

questions.prompt: A sampler calls random.Random(0) inside the loop that draws each parameter set. What is the consequence?
options: Nothing, since 0 is a valid seed
The samples are correlated but still cover the box
Every sample is identical, so there is no randomization
questions.explanation: Re-seeding with the same value resets the generator and reproduces the same numbers each time.

questions.prompt: Average cost over 5 plants is (0.4 + 0.5 + 0.45 + 0.5 + 1.15) / 5. What is the mean and what is the worst-case cost? Give the worst case. (two decimals)
questions.explanation: The mean is 0.60 but the worst case is 1.15, which a mean-only report would hide.

questions.prompt: Coverage of a 2-parameter box by 3 random samples that fall in 3 distinct cells of a 4 x 4 grid? (four decimals)
A real robot's payload turns out to be 5 kg, while the training box was 1 to 3 kg. Which diagnosis is most accurate?
options: Domain randomization failed, because it samples the parameters using random numbers
The deployment is outside the support of the training distribution, so no robustness is expected
The critic is overestimating the value of the policy at the heavier payload of 5 kg
The learning rate was too low, so the policy never covered the whole 1 to 3 kg box
questions.explanation: Randomization gives robustness only inside (and a little around) the sampled box.

questions.prompt: List three parameters you would randomize for a vision-based grasping policy trained in simulation, with a justification for each range.
rubric: Names plausible parameters (lighting, camera pose, object texture or mass, friction)
Gives a range or tolerance with a source
Notes one parameter to hold out or to test at the extremes
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Your randomized policy fails at the lightest, lowest-friction corner but works elsewhere. Give two possible causes and one experiment for each.
rubric: Corner outside the training box, or too few samples near it (coverage)
Gains too aggressive for the light plant (delay or damping), trade-off from heavier plants
Experiment: widen or add the corner to the box and re-test; or evaluate gains over a mass sweep
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: Write code or pseudocode for a coverage check of N parameter samples with k bins per axis and say what value should alarm you.
rubric: Maps each sample to a cell index per axis with clamping at the upper edge
Counts distinct cells divided by k^d
Alarm: a fraction far below 1 for the number of samples, or a very low fraction in high dimension
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

questions.prompt: You randomize mass and friction but not actuator latency, and the real robot oscillates. What is the most plausible explanation?
options: A dominant source of the gap (latency) was not randomized, so the policy never saw it
The mass range was too wide, so the policy became too cautious in its actions
Domain randomization cannot handle oscillation of any kind, whatever is randomized
The random seeds were identical, so no variation was actually sampled in training
questions.explanation: Robustness only covers the varied factors; unmodelled effects like delay need to be identified and randomized.
